description_full: Parex Resources Inc. engages in the exploration, development, production, and marketing of oil and natural gas in Colombia. Its principal land holdings and exploration blocks are located in the Llanos Basin, Magdalena Basin, and Putumayo Basin. The company was incorporated in 2009 and is headquartered in Calgary, Canada.

financial_summary: Parex Resources, Inc. is a small-cap energy business with a $1.4B market cap on $1.0B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -15% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are contracting by -9.7pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 25% against a 8% cost of capital — a 17-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 46%.

The business throws off $242M in free cash flow — roughly 24 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.67× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 80× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 9.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 2.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

news_headlines.title: Parex Resources (OTCMKTS:PARXF) Stock Breaks Below 200-Day Moving Average – Time to Sell?

sect: Its 25% operating margin runs 9pp above the Energy median (16%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 2.26x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.05 across 203 companies in the universe; the top four hold 40% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 61% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 20% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 34% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 45% and a beta of 0.61, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y -0.16 vs 5y 0.38), so read it loosely.
About $1.1M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 65% in the 2020 crash and 43% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 56% below its DCF fair value of $33.49, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 22%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $27.65 to $41.60 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Energy peers: P/E 2.4 vs 13.6, EV/EBITDA 3.4 vs 7.1 and P/FCF 5.8 vs 14.6 (sector median).
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 17.2% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 11.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 11.4% annual cash-flow growth, 16pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 25% clears the cost of capital of 8.0% by 17pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.66).
It runs a 46% gross margin and converts 24% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.67x.
ROE of 13% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.2x equity multiplier).
SG&A jumped 45% last year, worth watching.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $62.6M.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.8, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at -14.8% over 3 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
own: Insiders own a modest 1.6%, and institutions hold 54%.
It returns 9.5% a year to shareholders (1.9% in buybacks and 7.4% in dividends).
people: With about 461 employees, each generates about $2.2M of revenue, in line with the Energy median.
That works out to $524K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.2M (1x revenue per employee).
